analogs.note: Strong ocean signal + negative IOD offset → normal monsoon despite Super event.
Closest ocean-heat analog. Moderate drought; coupling locked in fully.
Coupling analog — peaked then faded fast. The cautionary precedent for 2026.
Subsurface heat present but coupling stalled; event underperformed.
Slow developer; weak coupling produced a low-amplitude event.
Big subsurface heat discharged by a June easterly burst; Super deferred to 2015.

analogInference: The analog set splits cleanly into two stories. On the ocean signal — subsurface heat and the Niño 3.4 trajectory — 2026 most resembles 1997 and 2015, the two sustained Super events. On the coupling signal — SOI and trade winds — it resembles 2023, which peaked and faded. The dashboard cannot resolve which story wins; that is precisely what the June–July atmospheric data will decide. The honest read: extraordinary ocean potential, unproven atmospheric follow-through. Weight 1997/2015 if coupling locks in, 2023 if it does not.

sources.name: NOAA CPC
sources.desc: Official US ENSO advisories, ONI, ENSO probabilities.

sources.name: IRI / Columbia
sources.desc: ENSO forecast plume, subsurface heat, model consensus.

sources.name: ECMWF
sources.desc: European ensemble — the bullish outlier on 2026 intensity.

sources.name: BOM (Australia)
sources.desc: Bureau of Meteorology ENSO Outlook, IOD tracking.

sources.name: India Met Dept
sources.desc: Official monsoon forecasts, onset, LPA distribution.

sources.name: Skymet Weather
sources.desc: Private Indian monsoon forecast; ENSO–monsoon analysis.

sources.name: NOAA NCEI
sources.desc: Global temperature records, annual ranking outlook.

sources.name: NOAA PMEL / TAO
sources.desc: Equatorial buoy array — trade winds, subsurface temps.

sources.name: NOAA PSL Climate Indices
sources.desc: Teleconnection and ocean indices in one place — NAO, AO, PNA, EA/WR, PDO, QBO, SOI, MEI, Niño regions, Indian-monsoon indices — many daily and back to 1948. The bridge from ENSO to actual circulation.

sources.name: ECMWF European Weather Regimes
sources.desc: Evolution of the Euro-Atlantic circulation regimes (+NAO, −NAO, blocking, Atlantic ridge). More analytically useful for a UK/Europe read than a raw temperature forecast.

sources.name: Climate Reanalyzer
sources.desc: Daily global SST anomalies, Niño 3.4, 500-hPa heights and jet maps — the fastest way to see the physical structure of an ongoing event rather than a single index.

sources.name: Copernicus C3S
sources.desc: ERA5 reanalysis and European climate monitoring — the continuous historical record needed to say how unusual an anomaly is against the 1950–present distribution.

sources.name: Met Office (UK)
sources.desc: UK climate monitoring, the NAO seasonal driver outlook, and rapid attribution studies estimating how warming shifted an event's probability.

sources.name: McNoldy RONI archive
sources.desc: Relative ONI monthly and seasonal values back to 1850, following CPC methodology — the source for locking exact historical RONI figures behind the Baseline & Rulers view.

sources.name: World Weather Attribution
sources.desc: Event-by-event attribution: how much more likely or intense a specific heatwave, drought or flood became because of anthropogenic warming — the climate-change layer of the analysis.
